omitted_axes.reason: The remediation changes persistence, lease CAS timing, typed projections and audit serialization, not an interactive UI.

test_cases.risk: PostgreSQL constraints may reject closed provider terminal outcomes, producing an untyped 500 and losing durable evidence.
test_cases.seam: PostgreSQL execution/reconciliation store and migration guards
prerequisites: Independent provider rejection, scope denial and reconciled request rejection fixtures.
PostgreSQL migration at the exact tested subject.
steps: Execute provider_request_rejected, provider_scope_denied and reconciled_request_rejected through execution and reconciliation.
Inspect persisted observations, terminal state, migrations and append-only audit after every transition.
Capture HTTP envelopes, write/effect counters and recursively scan public/audit evidence.
expected_results: provider_request_rejected is durable and maps to 502 TOOL_PROVIDER_REQUEST_FAILED.
provider_scope_denied is durable and maps to 403 TOOL_RESOURCE_ACCESS_DENIED, never indeterminate 202.
reconciled_request_rejected is durable and maps to 502 TOOL_PROVIDER_REQUEST_FAILED, without a constraint error, indeterminate 202, or untyped 500.
Only specified closed values are accepted; arbitrary provider text is rejected/redacted.
Safe failure_code is retained while rejection_code and raw provider material are absent.

test_cases.requirement: M4 fixed transaction-time lease and fencing
test_cases.risk: Moving database-clock reads can make lease/CAS decisions inconsistent inside one transaction.
test_cases.seam: PostgreSQL lease, fencing and stale-takeover transitions
prerequisites: A database harness that can advance the clock between statements without ending the transaction.
Current, foreign, stale and generation-mismatched owner fixtures.
steps: Exercise acquire, authorize/admit, observe, finalize and stale-takeover transitions under one transaction.
Race owners over the lock barrier and record the captured transaction timestamp, lease and generation values.
expected_results: Each transition uses one transaction_timestamp for lease comparisons, CAS predicates and transition timestamps.
Later wall-clock movement cannot change an in-flight classification.
Exactly one valid owner or strict-expiry takeover wins without duplicate effect; invalid owners are fenced.

test_cases.risk: Proposal reads and execution/reconciliation results may omit durable execution lifecycle state or leak trusted-store material.
prerequisites: Fixtures for success, terminal, indeterminate, in-progress, fenced and authority-denied outcomes.
steps: Create, read, execute and reconcile a proposal through both stores.
Reload the proposal and compare nested projection fields across every result.
Run the recursive public allowlist scan.
expected_results: Every current ToolProposalProjection includes sanitized execution lifecycle, generation, observations and terminal state where available.
Execution and reconciliation responses carry the same current nested proposal projection.
Provider IDs, routing handles, secrets, raw provider payloads, internal exceptions and rejection_code are absent recursively.
The projection survives reload and recovery and is sufficient for public lifecycle reconstruction.

test_cases.risk: Sanitization may erase the closed failure identity or leak the private rejection_code.
test_cases.seam: Append-only audit sanitizer and execution projection
prerequisites: Independent fixtures for target_not_found, validation_rejected, policy_rejected and the approved provider request-rejection code.
Both in-memory and PostgreSQL persistence paths.
steps: Run each closed terminal failure through execution and reconciliation.
Rebuild ordered audit from both stores after persistence and reload.
Validate the safe code and scan every nested public/audit value.
expected_results: Only validated safe failure_code remains in audit and the sanitized execution projection.
rejection_code, arbitrary provider errors, routing data, credentials and internal exceptions never appear.
The safe code survives PostgreSQL persistence, reload and HTTP serialization.
Unknown/unvalidated codes fail closed rather than being persisted or projected.
